svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.32 VENTILATION
Design and Installation

g.text: Ventilator in a service room, pictogram
System serving more than one unit, (4)
Section, schematic. Blue: supply, grey: return
Section, schematic. Article 3.1.8.10.(1): in the plane of
(2) Exhaust fans and supply fans: this Subsection
(1) For aspects not specifically described in this Subsection

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
Aspects of mechanical ventilation systems not
specifically described in this Subsection are
designed, constructed and installed in accordance
with good practice such as that described in the
ASHRAE Handbooks and Standards, the HRAI Digest the
HRAI Residential Mechanical Ventilation Manual, the
Hydronics Institute Manuals and the SMACNA Manuals.
Exhaust fans and supply fans are installed in
accordance with this Subsection and the
manufacturer’s instructions .
The mechanical components of a mechanical
ventilation system are installed so as to be
accessible for inspection, maintenance, repair, and
cleaning.
In a house with a secondary suite including their
common spaces, where a heating or ventilation system
serves more than a single dwelling unit, the system
is designed and installed to prevent the circulation
of smoke upon a signal from a duct-type smoke
detector.
Except as provided in Sentence 9.10.9.6.(14), ducts
penetrating fire separations are equipped with fire
dampers in conformance with Article 3.1.8.10.
(5) cites Sentence 9.10.9.6.(14). Article 9.10.9.6. has 2 Sentences. (1) "Digest the HRAI" and (2) "instructions ." as printed. Schematic.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.32.3.2. (page 9-289)
